mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For countries party to the Hague Apostille Convention: Notarize the certificate at the competent notary public in the country of origin, then obtain an Apostille from the designated competent authority (e.g., Ministry of Foreign Affairs or equivalent). For non-member states: Notarize the certificate, then legalize it through the consular section of the Republic of Korea Embassy or Consulate in the country of origin, followed by authentication by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and senior officers against the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) PEP list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the U.S. OFAC SDN List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Korean government's own sanctions list (Ministry of Foreign Affairs). Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required for any PEP, including foreign PEPs, family members, and close associates. Screening must be conducted at onboarding, on a continuous basis (at least daily for sanctions updates), and before any transaction. The screening process must include fuzzy matching, alias detection, and cross-referencing with multiple data sources. All results must be documented and retained for at least 5 years. For high-risk industries like medical device manufacturing, additional checks under the Korean Medical Devices Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act are required. Any positive hit must trigger immediate escalation to the compliance officer and, if necessary, a suspicious transaction report (STR) to KoFIU within 24 hours.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Korean Supreme Court Registry Office Online Name Clearance System (인터넷등기소 - 상호검색)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Korean (Hangul) script. For foreign entities, a phonetic transliteration into Hangul is required. The name must consist of a distinctive element, a business purpose descriptor, and a legal form suffix (e.g., 유한회사 for LLC). The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name. The four-tier naming convention includes: (1) distinctive name, (2) business purpose, (3) legal form, and (4) optional trade name. English names may be used as a secondary trade name but must be transliterated into Hangul for registration. The name must not contain any prohibited tokens or imply a false relationship with government agencies or public institutions.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety
Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name clearance application is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Korean Supreme Court Registry Office within 14 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must be submitted in writing, stating the grounds for appeal, and include a copy of the rejection notice and the original application. The Registry Office must review the appeal within 30 days and issue a written decision. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may further appeal to the administrative court within 90 days. Alternatively, the applicant may modify the proposed name and resubmit a new application. It is recommended to consult with a Korean licensed attorney (변호사) to prepare a strong appeal, especially if the rejection is based on similarity to an existing name. The appeal process is governed by the Administrative Litigation Act and the Commercial Registration Act.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a high-risk medical device manufacturing entity (intraocular lenses), a virtual office or commercial mailbox is strictly rejected by the Korean tax authorities (National Tax Service) and financial institutions. The entity must maintain a physical registered office in South Korea where the actual business operations, including manufacturing, quality control, and storage of medical devices, are conducted. The Korean Medical Devices Act (Act No. 18625) requires that manufacturers have a physical facility that meets Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) standards. The National Tax Service requires a physical place of business for VAT registration and corporate tax purposes. Banks will not open corporate accounts without a physical office inspection. Therefore, a virtual office is not permissible for this industry. The registered office must be a commercial space (not residential) and must be accessible for inspections.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced physical inspections: (1) Municipal tax office (구청) may inspect to verify business registration and actual operation; (2) National Tax Service (국세청) may conduct field audits for VAT and corporate tax compliance; (3) Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) may conduct GMP inspections and post-market surveillance; (4) Korean Customs Service may inspect for import/export compliance; (5) Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) may coordinate with tax authorities for AML inspections. Quantified risk: High (80% likelihood within the first year of operation) due to the high-risk classification of medical device manufacturing. The entity must maintain full operational records, employee presence, and physical inventory at the registered office. Any discrepancy may lead to administrative fines, license revocation, or criminal penalties.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), in particular Articles 543 through 590 concerning Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), and the Supreme Court Commercial Registration Rules; together with the Medical Devices Act for the regulated medical device manufacturing purpose.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Seoul Central District Court, under the National Court Administration of the Supreme Court of Korea; electronic filing is accepted through the Internet Registration Office and the district court registry window with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Corporation Registration (Bub-in Deung-gi Sincheongseo), filed together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation, capital deposit certificate, consents of the statutory officers, and supporting corporate instruments prescribed by the Commercial Registration Rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act of Korea. The incorporators may fix the initial capital at any amount; however, a customary initial paid-in capital of at least KRW 10,000,000 (approx. USD 7,450) is recommended for bank account opening, medical device licensing, and supplier credibility. The subscribed capital must be paid by cash deposit into a domestic commercial bank account in the name of the company before registration, and a certificate of deposit must be filed with the registry. No government-mandated blocked escrow account rule applies after registration; the funds are freely available for lawful business purposes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF YUHAN HOESA Date: [●], 20[●]; Place: Registered Office, Seoul, Republic of Korea. The undersigned, constituting all of the initial directors and statutory officers of Yuhan Hoesa, a limited liability company organized under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, do hereby waive notice of and convene the inaugural meeting of the Board of Directors. The Board notes that the Company was registered at the Commercial Registration Division, Seoul Central District Court, under Registration No. [●] on [●], and that its Articles of Incorporation and Certificate of Incorporation Registration have been inspected and found authentic. The Board acknowledges receipt of the deposit certificate issued by [●] Bank evidencing the payment of the initial capital contribution of KRW [●] into corporate account number [●] held in the name of the Company as of the date of incorporation. Upon review and deliberation, the Board unanimously resolves as follows: 1. Constitution of the Board. The Board ratifies the election of all directors and the appointment of the auditor, and confirms their qualifications under Articles 543 to 590 of the Commercial Act, the Medical Devices Act, and the Company's Articles of Incorporation. 2. The Board affirms that the initial members have validly subscribed for the issued capital of the Company and that the contribution of KRW [●] has been fully paid by cash deposit before registration. The Representative Director is authorized to cause the membership register to be executed, to issue contribution certificates or confirmatory entries, and to file all capital-related notices required by any Korean government authority. 3. The Representative Director and the Finance Director are jointly authorized to open demand deposit, savings, foreign currency, and letter-of-credit accounts; to execute checks, funds transfers, SWIFT payment orders, bank guarantees, letters of credit, and import/export settlement documents; and to bind the Company to routine banking transactions. Transactions exceeding USD 100,000 or KRW 100,000,000 require one additional signature or board preapproval.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax (https://www.hometax.go.kr) for corporate income tax, VAT, and business registration; customs export clearance and export declarations are processed through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system (https://unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity not yet registered in Korea, the entity must appoint a statutory Korean tax representative and file a foreign business operator registration application under the Value-Added Tax Act with the District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the tax representative or the place of establishment. Required submissions include the home-country certificate of incorporation, evidence of existence, power of attorney to the Korean tax representative, and a registration form detailing the business activity, expected taxable supplies, and no fixed place of business in Korea. Upon approval, the NTS issues a 10-digit Korean business registration number (TIN) and certifies the entity as a foreign business operator for VAT purposes. If the entity establishes a domestic Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), the entity completes commercial registration under the Commercial Act, then applies for a business registration certificate through HomeTax or the competent District Tax Office within 20 days from the commencement of business, obtaining the standard 10-digit business registration number used for corporate tax, VAT, and e-tax invoices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for entity classification; Korea has no check-the-box election and does not permit pass-through taxation for a limited liability company. A wholly-owned domestic subsidiary group may elect consolidated corporate income tax filing under the Corporate Tax Act if the statutory shareholding and other consolidated-filing qualification conditions are satisfied. Anti-hybrid mismatch classification is governed by the Tax Adjustment of International Transactions Act, not by elective entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold applies to a Korean corporate entity; VAT registration is mandatory from commencement of business or from the first taxable supply in Korea. For individual sole proprietors only, a simplified taxable person regime may apply when annual taxable turnover is not more than KRW 80,000,000; this simplification is not available to a Yuhan Hoesa corporation. A foreign non-resident supplier with no Korean establishment becomes subject to VAT registration from the first taxable supply, including electronically supplied services to Korean consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All Korean VAT current taxpayers must issue electronic tax invoices (e-tax invoices) transmitted to the NTS through HomeTax or an approved authorized service provider using the NTS tax-invoice API and prescribed XML schema. Electronic tax invoices must be transmitted no later than the day following the taxable supply. The NTS assigns a unique electronic tax invoice control number and maintains an anti-fraud transaction database, functioning as real-time fiscal clearance and digital stamping for each invoice. Failure to issue or transmit an e-tax invoice triggers statutory addition to tax under the Value-Added Tax Act. Foreign business operators use the HomeTax foreign business operator electronic tax invoice portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported goods qualify for the 0% VAT rate under the Value-Added Tax Act when the goods physically depart Korea as evidenced by an export customs declaration accepted in the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system, title and risk pass to a non-resident buyer, and the export proceeds are received in foreign currency and repatriated through a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank in accordance with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. For intraocular acrylic lenses, the zero-rating also depends on the underlying medical-device export being made by the Korean taxable business operator and not by a reseller without export processing. Qualifying offshore services supplied to non-residents and related to exported goods may also be zero-rated where the consideration is settled in cross-border foreign exchange transactions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration approved by the Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS electronic clearance (the Korean export clearance certificate equivalent to an export bill of entry)
Original Bill of Lading or Export Air Waybill consigned to the non-resident buyer and showing exit from a Korean seaport or airport

Foreign Exchange Receipt Certificate issued by a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing the inward remittance of export proceeds, being the Korean functional equivalent of an Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC)
Commercial Invoice, Packing List, and signed export sales contract or purchase order
Copy of the Korean automated customs export loading confirmation where required by NTS/KCS audit protocols
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and Korea Customs Service jointly verify the UNI-PASS export declaration, physical export documentation, and the foreign exchange receipt ledger. If export proceeds are not repatriated within the statutory 180-day basic deadline without an approved extension, or if documentation is incomplete, false, circular, or inconsistent with the declared export supply, the 0% rate is retrospectively denied and the supply is re-assessed at 10% VAT together with statutory addition to tax, interest for late payment, and possible denial or recoupment of any input VAT refund previously paid. Cases involving fabricated export declarations, forged e-tax invoices, or fraudulent offshore payment chains are referred for criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, with penalties including fines, imprisonment, and revocation of tax registrations. Export and VAT supporting records must be retained for at least five years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), with delegated foreign exchange administration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act co-administered by the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and Korea Customs Service
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalised market economy under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act: current account payments are generally unrestricted once routed through a designated foreign exchange bank, while capital account operations such as direct investment, overseas remittances and external borrowings require declaration, notification or ex-post reporting rather than prior licensing. KRW is convertible for underlying trade and business purposes, but international settlement must be executed in USD or EUR via SWIFT because offshore KRW clearing is limited and tightly monitored. Export proceeds no longer require mandatory surrender to the Bank of Korea; however, they must be collected within the statutory trade settlement period and repatriated to a domestic foreign currency account or converted at market rate. Dividend and profit remittance to a non-resident is lawful after final tax clearance, but the paying bank needs FIU-compliant corporate documents, audited financial statements and the FDI notification certificate to verify that profit is real and not disguised capital flight. Korean regulators aggressively review round-tripping, pre-payment imports and non-resident intercompany lending; all foreign capital injections must be reported to the designated bank before arrival and cannot be commingled with trade proceeds. Balance of payments reporting obligations declare quarterly external assets and liabilities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Trade Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, the exporter must collect export proceeds within 3 months of the date of exportation unless a written extension is granted by the Director of the relevant Customs Office; there is no mandatory percentage conversion to KRW; the exporter may retain 100% of the proceeds in a foreign currency account with an authorised foreign exchange bank, provided the bank is notified and the receipt is recorded under the corresponding export declaration. Overdue returns, write-offs, or settlements via unlicensed payment providers are treated as settlement violations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational KRW and USD Account
Capital Escrow Account / Export Proceeds Foreign Currency Account
Basic Operational Currency Account / LC and Trade Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account / Foreign Currency Clearing Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability - legally barred. No overseas fintech EMI is licensed as a foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, so it cannot open a corporate deposit account, clear KRW, or execute external payments on behalf of the Korean entity. A licensed EU or UK EMI can only act as a supporting agent or auxiliary service provider; all settlement and custody must pass through a Korean domestic deposit-taking bank. Operation through an unlicensed EMI would trigger bank-side suspicious transaction reporting, transaction freezing, regulatory sanctions, and a fatal AML defence weakness.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For this high-risk special-license medical device manufacturing entity, the statutory director and ultimate beneficial owner must attend at least one physical in-branch onboarding interview at the designated tier-1 commercial bank; remote video KYC is accepted only as an extra verification layer, not as a substitute. Remote consular proxy opening is not a recognised standard route without a fully apostilled power of attorney and prior enhanced due diligence; in practice, the bank compliance committee will require face-to-face confirmation of the business model, expected transaction lanes, and source of funds before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between non-resident UBO/signatory and Korean resident director or nominee governance structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport and legal register excerpt of every UBO, UBO declaration under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act, share ledger showing direct ownership, twelve-month personal or corporate bank statements proving source of funds, apostilled board resolution authorising the Korean representative, and an independent corporate structure diagram.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated LLC projecting unusually high intraocular lens export volume versus modest initial capital base
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: MFDS medical device licence, ISO 13485 and CE-MDR certification, notarised purchase orders from hospitals or distributors, UNI-PASS export declaration projections, lathe equipment purchase invoices, cleanroom environmental validation reports, audited or certified business plan, and reasoned revenue build-up model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Concentration of trade payments through third-country transhipping or alt-payment corridors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Denied-party screening results, end-customer declarations, Incoterms and trade contract files, original bills of lading and airway bills, freight forwarder KYC documents, customs import/export entries, warehouse inspection certificates, and payment trace showing direct payee identity consistent with invoices.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ambiguity in foreign equity capital injection routing, especially fronted loans or intermediary remitters
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign Investment Promotion Act notification certificate, designated bank foreign exchange registration record, inward remittance confirmation with exact purpose code, capital verification certificate issued by the bank, chain-of-title evidence from ultimate remitter through each intermediary, and an independent third-party AML legal opinion or forensic source-of-funds report.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign equity capital must be notified to the designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act before remittance; the inbound wire should be executed via SWIFT MT103 with the remitter identified as the foreign shareholder, the beneficiary as KR_YUHANGHOESA, and the purpose code referencing foreign direct investment rather than trade settlement. Upon receipt the bank issues a foreign exchange purchase/conversion certificate and an FDI registration confirmation, which is the capital verification evidence for the Korean corporate registry. The funds must remain in a dedicated capital escrow account until the paid-in capital entry is completed and the corporate bank account is fully activated; no commingling with operating revenue or trade proceeds is permitted.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements should run through the settled clearing rails that match the counterparty risk and instrument cycle: SWIFT MT103 for low-value resin and packaging suppliers, Commercial Letter of Credit (sight or usance) for high-value CNC lathe and hydrophobic acrylic material imports, and Documentary Collections (D/P or D/A) only where a complete original bill of lading and independent inspection certificate are attached. Every outward payment must be matched to a Korean customs export/import declaration in UNI-PASS, supported by purchase orders and invoices, and netted through the authorised foreign exchange bank accounts; KRW clearing is reserved solely for domestic purchases, with no use of offshore digital wallets or unlicensed payment channels.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward contracts: permitted only when supported by real underlying export/import exposure evidenced by invoices, LCs, or purchase orders, executed with a domestic FX-licensed bank and capped to the projected cash flow tenor.

FX swaps: permitted to hedge principal repatriation and timing mismatches between FDI injection, operational revenue conversion, and dividend remittance, provided all legs correspond to actual cross-border flows and no leverage is embedded.

Non-deliverable forwards: not permissible as a speculative instrument for this onshore Korean entity; any NDF access would require a documented genuine hedge and prior BOK/MOEF counterparty eligibility, and should otherwise be treated as a compliance red flag.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Corporate Tax Adjustment Return, Form 1021)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for calendar-year companies, by March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Underreporting penalty of 20% of the omitted tax (40% for fraudulent omission); delinquency interest of 0.025% per day (approximately 9.125% per annum) from the day after the due date; property seizure, business suspension, and criminal indictment under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act for repeated or substantial violations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Local Income Tax Return (Local Income Tax Surcharge on Corporate Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipal government of the company's registered principal place of business (Local Tax Office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after the corporate income tax return due date; for calendar-year companies, by April 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 5% for non-payment; overdue surcharge of 0.75% per month (9% per annum) for unpaid local income tax; compulsory collection through seizure of bank accounts and business assets

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Annual Operation Report (if any non-resident ownership exceeds 10%)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year, as required under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of up to KRW 1,000,000 (approximately USD 750) for failure to file; loss of foreign-investment tax incentives and legal protection; administrative strike-off risk for repeated non-compliance after registration of the investment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' Meeting Resolution and Financial Statement Approval, Retention, and Internal Availability
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed with a regulator; must be kept at the company's registered office and made available to shareholders and the Korean court upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (annual general meeting for a Yuhan Hoesa); financial statements must be kept for 10 years thereafter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of up to KRW 10,000,000 (approximately USD 7,500) under the Commercial Act for failure to conduct or record the annual general meeting; habitual non-compliance may lead to judicial dissolution of the company

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent CPA audit is triggered under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, and its Enforcement Decree, when a company (including a Yuhan Hoesa applying the same thresholds) has: (a) total assets exceeding KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 9,000,000); or (b) total assets exceeding KRW 7,000,000,000 (approximately USD 5,300,000) together with 30 or more employees; or (c) if designated by the External Audit Committee based on public interest factors such as total debt, sales, or number of shareholders.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) is mandatory for entities subject to external audit and for listed companies; non-listed small and medium companies that do not trigger the audit threshold may apply K-GAAP (General Corporate Accounting Standards, aligned with Korean SME GAAP) as long as they comply with the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information (AML/CFT), the company must maintain a current register of its beneficial owners and provide an updated UBO declaration to domestic financial institutions on an annual basis when conducting banking transactions. A transfer of shares representing 10% or more of the equity or voting rights must be reported to the company's principal financial institution within 30 days from the date of the transfer; additionally, if the investor is foreign, the transfer must be reported to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy through KOTRA within 30 days. The company must also update its internal shareholder register and, for foreign-investment purposes, reflect the new ownership in the next annual foreign-investment report. There is no separate government-wide annual UBO filing for a domestic Yuhan Hoesa, but any substantial ownership change must be recorded in the commercial registry if it alters the registered directors or company name.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 – USD 1,500 per year (no statutory registered agent is required in South Korea, but a physical registered office address and local accounting/correspondence services are customary; typical market quote for a registered office, mail handling and corporate secretarial support ranges within this band)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – USD 20,000 per year depending on total assets, revenue, transaction volume, and the complexity of intraocular lens export operations; mandatory large-company audits under the External Audit Act will generally command the higher part of this range.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9% on first KRW 200 million of taxable income; 19% on KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 21% on KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; 24% above KRW 300 billion
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday. Preferential deductions and credits are available for R&D expenditures, high-tech medical device facility investment, job creation, and foreign direct investment in free economic zones. Eligible FDI can obtain a 100% corporate income tax exemption for the first 5 years and a 50% reduction for the next 2 years. Additional credits apply to investments in new growth industry technologies such as intraocular lens manufacturing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return on Tax Base and Tax Amount, together with Local Income Tax Surtax Return, attached financial statements and supplementary schedules; electronically filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal (hometax.go.kr).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return with semi-annual interim tax prepayment obligations
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final corporate income tax return must be filed within 3 months after the fiscal year-end. A December 31 fiscal year-end therefore requires filing by March 31 of the following year. Interim tax prepayment returns are due within 2 months after the first half of the fiscal year, generally by August 31.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity name, foreign ownership percentage, fiscal year start date and end date, tax identification number, business code and statutory place of management or Korean permanent establishment indicator.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Korean tax identification number and clearly indicate whether the company is a domestic corporation or a foreign corporation with a Korean permanent establishment. Foreign shareholders should list their country of residence and DTA jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All Korean-source and global revenue realized by the domestic corporation, including sales from precision lathe turning of foldable hydrophobic cataract lenses and related device components.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident taxpayer, include only Korean-source income attributable to the Korean permanent establishment. Offshore intra-group raw material purchases are separately reported in the international transactions schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 03 / Non-Taxable Income and Deductible Expense Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-taxable revenues, excluded dividends, deductible reserves and allowances, depreciation adjustments, entertainment expense limitations and any transfer pricing corrections made in accordance with Korean domestic rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses attributable to exempt Korean income or to an offshore branch not constituting a permanent establishment are non-deductible. DTA provisions restricting Korean taxing rights must be claimed through a separate withholding treaty claim and supporting tax residence certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of prior-year net operating losses carried forward against current-year taxable income before applying progressive corporate tax rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforward is limited to 10 years for general corporations and 15 years for qualifying small and medium-sized enterprises. A foreign corporation may only deduct losses previously reported and documented in Korea through its permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 05 / Taxable Income and Tax Rate Application
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of normal corporate tax using the progressive brackets and any adjusted income due to transfer pricing modifications.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the taxpayer's only Korean activity is a limited agency arrangement without a permanent establishment, no corporate return is required and the payer must instead withhold tax on Korean-source income. If a permanent establishment exists, compute tax on Korean-source business profits as adjusted under the applicable DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of foreign tax credits, R&D tax credits, employment and facility investment credits, and treaty relief granted as direct reductions of corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are available for foreign taxes paid on foreign-source income. DTA-based withholding exemptions must be documented by the beneficial owner's tax residence certificate and filed with the withholding agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 07 / Corporate Tax Payable and Local Income Tax Surtax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final national corporate income tax after all credits and the 10% local income tax surtax imposed on the national corporate tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign corporation with a Korean permanent establishment pays both national corporate tax and local income tax surtax through the annual return. Distributions of profits to non-resident shareholders are separately subject to dividend withholding tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing triggers additional tax of 20% of the unpaid tax, increased to 40% for fraudulent concealment. Underreporting or failure to report triggers 10% to 40% of the understated tax. Unpaid tax accrues daily additional tax of 0.025% per day until settlement. Criminal tax penalties may apply for wilful evasion, including imprisonment and fines of up to three times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate withholding on dividends paid to a non-resident corporate shareholder, composed of 20% national corporate income tax withholding plus 2% local income tax surtax
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain reduced or zero DTA withholding rates, the non-resident beneficial owner must deliver a valid Tax Residence Certificate issued by the foreign tax authority to the Korean withholding agent before payment, together with a statement of beneficial ownership and Form for Treaty Application for Reduction or Exemption of Withholding Tax. The withholding agent files the documents with the Korean tax office through HomeTax and applies the treaty rate at remittance. Where treaty relief was not applied at payment, the non-resident may file a refund claim with the competent Korean regional tax office within the statutory refund period, generally 5 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Licensing royalties paid to a non-resident are subject to 22% aggregate statutory withholding (20% national plus 2% local), with treaty rates typically ranging from 0% to 15% depending on jurisdiction. Interest on cross-border loans carries the same 22% statutory aggregate withholding; applicable DTA interest rates generally range from 10% to 15%. Treaty relief requires the beneficial owner to prove real economic substance, legal entitlement and that the interest or royalty is not disguised equity.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File: annual revenue of KRW 100 billion or more. Local File: annual revenue of KRW 100 billion or more and cross-border related-party transaction amounts of KRW 50 billion or more in the preceding fiscal year. Country-by-Country Report: consolidated group annual revenue of KRW 1 trillion or more. All KRW thresholds apply per Korean fiscal year.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not apply a narrow Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations regime, but Korean tax law applies the substance-over-form doctrine, general anti-abuse rules, controlled foreign corporation rules, beneficial ownership tests and real economic activity standards to prevent treaty shopping and thin capitalization. A Korean Yuhan Hoesa distributing intraocular acrylic lens profits must demonstrate actual staff, offices, decision-making, inventory risk and operational substance; passive shell or conduit arrangements will be disregarded or recharacterized.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion through False or Non-Filed Corporate Returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful omission of Korean-source revenue from lens manufacturing, issuance of false tax invoices, fabrication of deductible operating expenses, or concealment of offshore accounts receiving wire transfer proceeds for intraocular lens shipments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment for up to 3 years and a fine of up to 3 times the evaded tax under Korean tax punishment statutes; aggravated criminal liability for evasion amounts exceeding KRW 500 million; civil additional tax of 40% plus daily surcharges of 0.025% per day.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Representative directors who instruct, approve or knowingly benefit from evasion are subject to criminal fines, imprisonment, exit and travel bans, and civil restitution of the evaded tax with interest. Korean courts routinely pierce the corporate veil where funds are diverted to shareholder personal accounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company or Conduit Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Korean Yuhan Hoesa with no real employees, production facility, bank risk management or decision-making substance as a booking vehicle; routing intraocular lens royalties or dividends to a tax-haven intermediary to bypass Korean DTA limitations; inconsistent transfer pricing margins for acrylic lens manufacturing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of treaty benefits, recharacterization of transactions under the substance-over-form doctrine, transfer pricing adjustment, penalties of 10% to 30% of the adjusted tax amount, and denial of refund applications. Korean Customs and tax authorities may also impose additional import valuation adjustments on lens components supplied by foreign affiliates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly liable for unpaid corporate taxes when corporate formalities are ignored, assets are stripped from the company, or income is attributed to a paper foreign subsidiary. Directors can face asset freeze orders, civil damages to creditors, and criminal prosecution for aiding fraudulent tax structures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Cross-Border Payment Irregularities in High-Risk Medical Device Trade
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence on SWIFT wire or letter-of-credit payments, receipt of funds from sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions without a beneficial ownership audit, splitting large lens export proceeds into smaller unreported transfers, or laundering proceeds through personal accounts of the representatives.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Financial Transactions Reports and Speculative Transactions Act, failure to submit a suspicious transaction report is punishable by imprisonment for up to 5 years or a fine of up to KRW 50 million. Money laundering offenses carry forfeiture of proceeds, monetary penalties, and license suspension or revocation of the statutory medical device manufacturing license. Regulators may also impose administrative sanctions against the licensed manufacturer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Compliance officers and directors with supervisory authority face criminal liability where AML reporting was wilfully bypassed. Directors may be banned from re-entering South Korea or from serving as a corporate officer, their assets subject to civil forfeiture, and principal offenders are imprisoned.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Incorrect International Transaction Reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or submit Master File, Local File, Country-by-Country Report or the annual cross-border related-party transaction report where thresholds are met; use of non-arm's length manufacturing margins for intraocular lens sales; failure to provide contemporaneous comparability analysis for acrylic lens component procurement or trademark royalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing assessment of the profit margin using the most reliable comparable data, additional tax equal to the difference computed at the statutory corporate tax rates, penalty of up to 20% on the underreported income for absence of documentation, up to 30% penalty for grossly inaccurate international transaction reports, and daily additional tax on unpaid assessments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly cause the omission of international transaction reporting bear personal criminal exposure and can be fined or imprisoned. The Korean tax authority may hold the director personally responsible for penalties where the company is dissolved, insolvent or used as a conduit for punitive tax positions.
